title: Decisions for the Icelandic word lists

entities.title: Build the bluff-the-definition game (dropped)
entities.summary: Phase 1 of an Icelandic bluff-the-definition game produced 1,800 verified rare words with difficulty levels. The owner then dropped the game because an Icelandic edition of such a game already exists; the word list is kept in data/rare-words.json, unused.
entities.context: The owner asked for the game in two phases and for Phase 2 not to start until Phase 1 is approved. Phase 1 had to show at least 200 verified words that are real, obscure, not given away by their parts, short to define and suitable. The owner then asked for difficulty levels, the easiest playable with children, and for a larger list to fill them.

options.title: GO
options.consequences: Phase 2 builds the game: lobby with room code, rounds, voting, scoring, reveal with source link, big-screen view, reconnects, custom words.

options.title: Revise the list first
options.consequences: The owner or another native speaker reviews the sample and the uncertain wording; words are dropped or reworded before the build.

entities.origin: The owner's request for the game, in a Claude Code session, 23 November 2026

entities.decision: Not built. The folder was repurposed for word lists for other party games.

entities.title: Difficulty levels as windows on a 1–10 word difficulty score
entities.summary: For the rare-word list (data/rare-words.json): every word has a difficulty score 1–10 and a level is a [min, max] window on it. Kept for reference; no game uses the list.
entities.context: The owner asked for difficulty levels: the lowest playable with children, the highest holding the obscure words of the first round, with each level setting minimum and maximum word difficulty on a bell curve.
entities.decision: Proposed windows, stored in research/words.json under erfidleikastig: Barnvænt 1–4 (child-friendly only), Létt 2–6, Miðlungs 4–8, Erfitt 6–10. The windows are data and can be changed without touching the words.
entities.rationale: Overlapping windows give every level enough words (537–1,408) and let the owner tune levels without re-scoring.
entities.decidedBy: The owner (the approach); the windows are a proposal
entities.origin: The owner's request in a Claude Code session, 23 November 2026

entities.title: Words known only inside a trade are fair game
entities.summary: A word that farmers, sailors, weavers or clergy know but most people outside the trade don't counts as obscure; it is scored by how many people in the general adult population know it.
entities.context: Raised when reviewing sheep-farming words in Phase 1.
entities.decision: Domain-specific words are allowed at every level, scored by general-population familiarity.
entities.origin: The owner's message in a Claude Code session, 23 November 2026

entities.title: Word lists for six party-game mechanics
entities.summary: Build original Icelandic lists for a code-clue team game, a grid-clue game, an outsider game, a describe-around-traps game, a category race and a one-syllable describing game, without copying any published game's cards.
entities.context: The owner listed six word, clue and bluffing games with no known Icelandic edition and asked for good word lists for all of them.
entities.decision: One reviewed list of common nouns with per-game suitability fields serves the four clue/describe games; separate original lists serve the outsider game (16-word topic grids) and the category race (prompts with example answers); a one-syllable word-form list supports the one-syllable game.
entities.rationale: The four clue games all need well-known nouns and differ only in which properties matter (associations, concreteness, describability), so one list with fields avoids duplicate review work.
entities.decidedBy: The owner (the goal); the structure is a proposal
entities.origin: The owner's message in a Claude Code session, 23 November 2026
